title: Identification of SNP Targeted Pathways From Genome-wide Association Study \(GWAS) Data
protocol: Set up necessary environment to run PANOGA.
Download the PANOGA files from http://akademik.bahcesehir.edu.tr/~bbgungor/panoga_protocol.zip.
Unzip the downloaded PANOGA_protocol.zip file and extract it.
Create a folder with your disease name under PANOGA_protocol/data/.
Create a folder with your disease name under PANOGA_protocol/out/.
Format GWAS results input file following the instructions provided.
Save this formatted file under PANOGA_protocol/data/$DISEASE_NAME/.
Run the java script "createpanogainput.jar" to create four input files.
Replace $INPUT_FILE_NAME with your input file name.
Replace $DISEASE_NAME with your disease name.
Replace $PVALUE_THRESHOLD with the genotypic p-value threshold for SNP restriction.
Use the command: java -jar createpanogainput.jar $INPUT_FILE_NAME $DISEASE_NAME $PVALUE_THRESHOLD.
Go to the SPOT webserver at https://spot.cgsmd.isi.edu/submit.php.
Click into “Upload SNP File” button; select the SPOT input file, i.e., $DISEASE_NAME_spot_input.txt.
Change “Maximum SNPs to output:” parameter to 50,000 in SPOT webserver.
If your $PVALUE_THRESHOLD (from Step 6) is different than 0.05, change it in the “p-value threshold:” parameter of SPOT webserver.
Select the appropriate HAPMAP sample among the available options in SPOT webserver under “Linkage Disequilibrium (LD) options”.
Click into “Run” button and download the result under “Primary Results” section.
Save the SPOT output as Tab-delimited file under PANOGA_protocol/data/$DISEASE_NAME/$DISEASE_NAME_spot_output.txt.
Proceed with the full PANOGA procedure.
Run the java script “parsespotoutput.jar” to get a list of gene symbols assigned into typed SNPs.
Type the following command to perform functional enrichment of identified gene symbols:
Replace $DISEASE_NAME below with the disease name that you specified in Step 3.
Install Cytoscape version 2.6.3 by following its installation guide.
Install jActiveModules and ClueGO version 1.4 plugins into Cytoscape_v2.6.3/plugins/.
Replace $DISEASE_NAME with the disease name specified in Step 3 and run:
java -jar runfsnp.jar $DISEASE_NAME
Go to the SNPnexus webserver at: http://www.snp-nexus.org/.
Under “Batch Query” option, browse SNPnexus input file.
Select "Conserved Transcription Factor Binding Sites (TFBS)" under "Annotation Categories" -> "Regulatory Elements".
Click "Run" button.
Download the result under the “Regulatory Elements” section via clicking into TXT icon.
Save the SNPnexus output as a text file under PANOGA_procedure/data/$DISEASE_NAME/$DISEASE_NAME_snpnexus_output.txt.
Go to the SNPinfo webserver at: http://snpinfo.niehs.nih.gov/snpfunc.htm.
Browse and upload SNPinfo input file, i.e., $DISEASE_NAME_snpinfo_input.txt.
Click “Submit” button and download the results via clicking into “Export To Excel” button under “SNP Function Prediction Results”.
Save the SNPInfo output as a csv file under PANOGA_procedure/data/$DISEase_NAME/$DISEASE_NAME_snpinfo_output.csv.
Replace $DISEASE_NAME with the disease name specified in Step 3 to run “combinespotfsnp.jar” to combine SPOT and F-SNP output files.
Run “incorporatesnpnexus.jar” to incorporate functional information from SNPnexus.
Decide which human protein-protein interaction dataset to use as the initial network—follow option A for default or B for customized PPI network.
Run Cytoscape.exe for Windows users.
Run ./cytoscape.sh for Linux users.
Import network data from a local computer into Cytoscape.
Assemble network data into a SIF file.
Import human PPI network using File->Import->Network commands in Cytoscape.
Load gene attributes to nodes using File->Import->Attribute/Expression Matrix commands in Cytoscape and selecting the gene attributes file.
Select SPOTPvaluesig and FSScorePvaluesig from Expression Attributes panel.
Set “Number of Modules” parameter to 1000 in General Parameters panel.
Click “Find Modules” to identify active sub-networks.
Save the result as text file into PANOGA_procedure/data/$DISEASE_NAME/$DISEASE_NAME_jactivemodules_output.txt via clicking into “Save All Results” button on “Results Panel”.
Create a folder with your disease name under PANOGA_protocol/ClueGO/data/.
Create a folder with your disease name under PANOGA_protocol/ClueGO/out/.
Run “parsejactivemodulesoutput.jar” to create individual files containing gene symbols for each identified sub-network.
Replace $DISEASE_NAME in the command with the specified disease name.
Decide which pathway resource to use for functional enrichment of subnetworks.
Assign genes into KEGG pathways by following option A in ClueGO properties file.
Change "SelectedOntologySources" to "KEGG_14.03.2012" in clueGO.props file.
Assign genes into Biocarta pathways by following option B in ClueGO properties file.
Change "SelectedOntologySources" to "REACTOME_BioCarta_07.04.2011" in clueGO.props file.
Windows users type the command: java –jar functionalenrichment.jar $DISEASE_NAME $NUMBER_OF_SUBNETWORKS
Linux users perform similar command according to their system configuration.
Run the java script “combinesubnetworkpathways.jar” using the following command: >java –jar combinesubnetworkpathways.jar $DISEASE_NAME $NUMBER_OF_SUBNETWORKS
Create a directory under PANOGA_protocol/out/ for storing gene attribute files by typing the following commands:
>cd out/KeggPathwayMapGeneAttributeFiles
>mkdir $DISEASE_NAME
>cd ..
Run the java script "createattributesforpathwaymap.jar" to create a gene attributes file for each identified pathway.
Replace $DISEASE_NAME with the disease name specified in Step 3.
Execute the command: >java –jar createattributesforpathwaymap.jar $DISEASE_NAME
Save gene attribute files under PANOGA_protocol/out/KeggPathwayMapGeneAttributeFiles/$DISEASE_NAME for each identified sub-network.
Color SNP targeted genes for the pathway of interest using KEGG Mapper – Color Pathway tool.
Type “hsa” followed by the KEGG Term ID for the pathway of interest in the “Select KEGG pathway map:” field.
Obtain KEGG Term IDs from the first column of the $DISEASE_NAME_pathways_subnetwork_genes.csv file under PANOGA_procedure/out/$DISEASE_NAME/.
Browse gene attribute file created in Step 39 for the pathway of interest.
Hit “Execute” button to generate a customized pathway map where SNP targeted genes are colored based on the number of SNPs per base pair.
